_note: Why each one-off measurement was taken and what it produced. Status is one of: stands, superseded, withdrawn, invalid. A withdrawn entry is kept because knowing a measurement was wrong is worth more than not knowing it existed.

bench_activation_ladder.question: Does the same model cost the same to load on every node?
bench_activation_ladder.why: Every cross-arm comparison assumes trials are comparable. If node identity moves the number, pooling arms collected on different nodes is invalid — and most of this project's campaigns were collected opportunistically across whatever hardware was free.
bench_activation_ladder.produced: Cold boot for one identical 68.3 GB model ranged 344–1372 s across 8 nodes — a 4.0x spread — while wake stayed 1.43–2.07 s and park cost 113.5–115.8 GiB.
bench_activation_ladder.claim: Node identity dominates absolute load cost; retention converts a high-variance cost into a near-constant one.
bench_activation_ladder.note: This is the origin of the never-pool rule. It is the single most load-bearing measurement in the archive for how everything else must be read.

bench_activated_residency.question: Does holding a parsed EAM potential in a live process actually avoid the re-parse? (E1/E2)
bench_activated_residency.why: The whole data-side mechanism rests on it. If LAMMPS memoised the tabulation internally, retention would be a no-op and there would be no contribution.
bench_activated_residency.produced: r1_parse_cold 44.90 s, r2_parse_warm 42.83 s, r3_reuse_live 4.78 s, r4_repeat_coeff 42.84 s. Activated size 16.93 GB — a 5.10x expansion of the 3.32 GB file.
bench_activated_residency.claim: Retention is worth 9.0x on reuse, and LAMMPS does NOT memoise — re-issuing pair_coeff costs a full re-parse. The saving is unavailable by accident; it requires an explicit resident worker.
bench_activated_residency.note: The r4 arm is what makes this a contribution rather than a configuration flag. It also corrected an earlier ~9.8 GB estimate — do not cite that figure.

verify_persistent_lammps.question: Does a persistent worker preserve the physics?
verify_persistent_lammps.why: A retention speedup that changes the answer is not a speedup.
verify_persistent_lammps.produced: 93.73 s to 10.56 s per redundant invocation (8.88x), potential energy relative difference 0.000e+00.
verify_persistent_lammps.claim: Activated-data retention is bit-identical in its output.
verify_persistent_lammps.note: Single-node. The retention RATIO itself moves with the node (8.96x / 10.71x / 11.29x / 11.39x measured across three), so quote this with its node named.

bench_format_activation.question: How much does retention buy per gigabyte held, and does it depend on the format?
bench_format_activation.why: A budget has to rank resources against each other. Ranking needs a per-GB value, and it is only usable if it is a property of the format rather than of the instance.
bench_format_activation.produced: Seconds-per-GB spread 65x across formats (ASCII ~22.0 down to npy ~0.34), flat to within 1.00–1.16x across a 4x size range within each format.
bench_format_activation.claim: s/GB is a format constant, so it can be measured once and cached; and models land in the MIDDLE of the data range, so no fixed class priority is correct.
bench_format_activation.note: Feeds fig-sgb-spread. Note the paper prose and the figure read DIFFERENT files — one node-specific, one not.

bench_potential_activation.question: Of the cost of making a potential usable, how much is I/O and how much is parse?
bench_potential_activation.why: It decides whether a byte-oriented prefetcher could help at all. Staging bytes early can only recover the I/O share.
bench_potential_activation.produced: Cold load 100.10 s, warm load 98.23 s, raw sequential read 4.78 s, with mincore-verified cache state at every rung.
bench_potential_activation.claim: I/O is 1.9% of the cost; 98.1% is parse and spline construction inside the consumer. Staging the bytes recovers at most 1.9%.
bench_potential_activation.note: Replaced an earlier '129 s load / 106 s parse' figure that was extrapolated from a Python parse rate. LAMMPS parses in C++; do not cite the old numbers.

bench_wake_L1_coherence_32b.question: Does a level-1 sleep wake up CORRECT, not merely fast?
bench_wake_L1_coherence_32b.why: Level-2 sleep produced verbatim garbage on this cluster while returning HTTP success. A footprint or latency number from an engine that wakes broken is worthless.
bench_wake_L1_coherence_32b.produced: Cold boot 782.27 s, wake 2.076 s, verbatim-correct output at both warm and cache-evicted rungs, throughput unchanged (20.05 vs 20.20 tok/s). Park cost 120.77 GiB for a 68.28 GB model = 1.90x.
bench_wake_L1_coherence_32b.claim: L1 parking is real and coherent, and 377x cheaper than a cold boot. The degeneracy is an L2-only pathology.
bench_wake_L1_coherence_32b.note: The coherence probe is why this is trustworthy and the L2 result was not.

bench_sleep_wake_qwen_72b_instruct.question: Earlier attempt at the same sleep/wake ladder.
bench_sleep_wake_qwen_72b_instruct.produced: L1 and L2 timings in one process.
bench_sleep_wake_qwen_72b_instruct.note: Its L2 arm is CONTAMINATED: L1 cycles ran first in the same process and never released the host-side backup, so the 'L2' wake had L1's copy resident. Do not use its L2 numbers.

bench_l2_pressure.question: What does level-2 sleep cost in host memory?
bench_l2_pressure.claim: Superseded by the L1 coherence work.

bench_residency_preflight.question: How many engines can be parked at L1 simultaneously? (Stage-0 gates a and b)
bench_residency_preflight.why: If everything fits, there is no arbitration problem and no paper.
bench_residency_preflight.produced: k=1 parked at 197.5 GiB host RAM, k=2 at 305.6 GiB, k=3 did not complete (timeout on Blackwell, HTTP 500 on L40S). Delta 108–128 GiB per engine.
bench_residency_preflight.claim: Something must decide what NOT to park — parking everything is not available at a realistic allocation.
bench_residency_preflight.note: Two over-reads to avoid. The k=3 failure was a timeout and an HTTP 500, NOT an observed OOM or node death. And the fleet was four copies of ONE 32B model, not the four distinct agent models.

bench_preactivation_interference.question: Does background pre-activation slow the foreground agent? (E3)
bench_preactivation_interference.why: If speculative work costs foreground throughput, the scheduler must trade CPU against RAM and the decision variable is two-dimensional.
bench_preactivation_interference.produced: Eight concurrent background parsers burning ~8 of 12 cores changed the foreground median by 0.001 s (0.618 to 0.618 s). Verified genuinely running: 46.41 CPU-seconds in 6 s of wall.
bench_preactivation_interference.claim: CPU leaves the policy. The scheduler budgets RAM only, which is what makes seconds-per-GB a complete decision variable.
bench_preactivation_interference.note: The instrumentation matters — a flat curve is also the signature of a probe that silently did nothing, which is how the L2 result was misread. Bounded claim: every level tested was under-subscribed with small working sets.

bench_cow_prefork.question: Can a template process parse once and fork a child per tool call, sharing the tables copy-on-write?
bench_cow_prefork.why: It would be strictly better than a resident worker — a fresh process each call, so no residue and no segfault risk to the retained state.
bench_cow_prefork.produced: fork_noop 0.227 GB private-dirty, fork_read_only 0.227 GB, prefork_child 0.649 GB against a 0.46 GB table = 92% dirtied. Flat at f = 0.921–0.950 across a 4x scale sweep, THP on and off, and both pair styles.
bench_cow_prefork.claim: Copy-on-write collapses the instant LAMMPS runs, because run() re-runs the spline interpolation and rewrites every coefficient array in place. Prefork is dead for this consumer; a resident worker re-interpolates into the SAME memory and stays 1x.
bench_cow_prefork.note: Killed a design I had recommended, before any of it was built. The negative control (write_control) is what makes the null result trustworthy — without it, a blind probe would have looked identical.

bench_h1_quantized_park.question: Does quantisation halve the parked footprint of a 72B? (H1)
bench_h1_quantized_park.why: Every cell where arbitration is worth >=20% assumes it does. It was the last unmeasured assumption under the policy claim.
bench_h1_quantized_park.produced: Job SIGKILLed by a 4 GiB per-user cgroup cap on the login node.

bench_h1_fp8_tp1.question: Same question, retried on a compute node with online fp8.
bench_h1_fp8_tp1.produced: Boot 954.99 s, park 82.04 GiB. But the coherence probe returned 'は.   1111' for 'The capital of France is'.
bench_h1_fp8_tp1.claim: NONE — the engine was incoherent. A footprint from a broken engine describes tensors of the right size in an engine that does not work.
bench_h1_fp8_tp1.note: Two lessons. Online --quantization fp8 of this model at tp=1 on Blackwell produces garbage. And the coherence rule that let it through checked only for non-empty text plus a finish_reason — the verbatim '!!!!' degeneracy it was written to catch passes that too. Only a semantic anchor catches it. H1 remains UNMEASURED.

bench_v0_park_column.question: Which memory column does an L1 park actually land in?
bench_v0_park_column.why: The fp8 run parked 82 GiB entirely in the cgroup's file column with anon unmoved. If that is what parking really does, then reading anon reports held_gb = 0.0 for a real park — which would tell the arbitrator that holding a model is free and void every retention decision.
bench_v0_park_column.produced: Coherent fp16 32B: anon unchanged at 3.32 GiB, file 0.57 to 114.61 GiB (+114.04), VRAM 84023 to 1293 MiB. Park 122.09 GB, ratio 1.79x. Sleep 75.974 s then 1.346 s.
bench_v0_park_column.claim: An L1 park lands entirely in the file column on a coherent engine. The charging column must be anon + file.
bench_v0_park_column.note: Also confirms the fp8 result was not a broken-engine artifact.

bench_v0b_park_backing.question: Is that file-backed park a real file on storage, or memory the kernel merely files under an inode?
bench_v0b_park_backing.why: This decides a paper-level claim. cgroup v2 accounts BOTH real page cache and tmpfs/shm under 'file'. If the park is storage-backed it is a file range a byte-oriented tier could stage, and the argument that a DMSH structurally cannot express model residency weakens.
bench_v0b_park_backing.produced: All 114.18 GiB of the park is /dev/zero (deleted) mappings — 24 of them. Storage-backed memory in the entire process tree totals 0.907 GiB, which is code and libraries.
bench_v0b_park_backing.claim: The park never touches storage. MAP_SHARED over /dev/zero gives the kernel an internal shmem inode, which is why it is charged to file. The rung-coverage argument SURVIVES — only the word 'anonymous' was wrong. Correct phrasing is 'process-owned memory with no storage backing'.
bench_v0b_park_backing.note: The 114.18 / 0.907 GiB split is the whole argument in one measurement.

bench_residency_data_worker.question: Does the resident data worker retain, release, and preserve physics? (D1/D2/D4)
bench_residency_data_worker.why: D2 is the item most likely to fail silently: a worker that retains but cannot truly release makes the budget a fiction and every downstream percentage meaningless.
bench_residency_data_worker.produced: D1 warm parse 90.12 s vs live reuse 7.91 s = 11.39x. D2 proven four ways: release() returned 17.9334 GB measured as Private_Dirty; the job cgroup independently went 18.4182 to 0.0155 GB; the process left /proc; and re-activation afterwards cost 89.769 s. D4 pe relative difference 0.000e+00. One thread at worker startup against 193 unpinned.
bench_residency_data_worker.claim: Option-4 residency works, and eviction is real rather than asserted.
bench_residency_data_worker.note: The behavioural check is the one that matters — the saving is gone after release, which it could not be if release had freed nothing. Also found that an in-process close() alone freed 17.75 GB at full size but only 0.084 of 0.364 GB at small scale, so an in-process-only release would have looked broken when small and fine when large.

bench_p1_*.question: Which consumer library and dataset can supply an exogenously-sized activated artifact? (Gate P1/P2/P3)
bench_p1_*.why: The policy sweep said a cost-aware ranking needs >=34 GB of activated data to beat LRU. The EAM potential activates to 16.93 GB and its size is a knob we turn, which makes it an illustration rather than a regime.
bench_p1_*.produced: pyhmmer activation share flat at 46–49% across a 40x size range, expansion 2.27–2.31x. UniRef90: 60.95 GB on disk to 117.20 GB activated (1.923x), cold 420.8 s, s/GB 3.179, rungs verified distinct. Parquet, sprot, UniRef50 measured alongside.
bench_p1_*.claim: UniRef90 is the only artifact measured that clears both design thresholds, and its size is set by UniProt rather than by us.
bench_p1_*.note: s/GB 3.18 sits INSIDE the model band (2.78–3.81), which is what makes it the first resource that genuinely contests budget with a model. The EAM potential at 2.25 is below the band and loses at any size.

diag_p1_superlinear_8gb.question: Why did pyhmmer load time scale 47x for 4x more data?
diag_p1_superlinear_8gb.why: On its face it promoted pyhmmer to the lead candidate. A 12x collapse in parse rate is far more likely to be an artifact than a format property, and acting on it unchecked would have redirected the workload pivot.
diag_p1_superlinear_8gb.produced: Same 8 GB file, same node, two filesystems: Lustre scratch 568.3 s at 14.1 MB/s with the rate decaying 16.3x within a single read; node-local NVMe 52.2 s at 153.3 MB/s, flat.
diag_p1_superlinear_8gb.claim: The superlinearity was STORAGE CONTENTION, not allocator or structure degradation. The 91.8% activation share and 12.13x speedup derived from it are WITHDRAWN — the corrected figure is ~47.6%, in line with the 46–49% format constant.
diag_p1_superlinear_8gb.note: The secondary finding outlived the verdict: shared-filesystem rebuild cost can collapse an order of magnitude, which is the data-axis twin of the 4.0x node spread in cold boot. It also made node-local /tmp mandatory for every data-axis timing — fadvise is a silent no-op on Lustre, so cold-vs-warm rungs measured there are two identically-cached rungs.

analyze_misses.question: Of the stall a retention policy could address, how much is actually addressable?
analyze_misses.why: A ranking can only convert REPLACEMENT misses. Compulsory and capacity misses are immune to any policy.
analyze_misses.produced: At the 256 GB production budget: replacement misses are 10 of 209 and 2.6% of stall seconds; 46.0% is compulsory and 51.4% is capacity.
analyze_misses.claim: At the allocation actually used, the category a smarter policy can convert is small — which is why quantisation (H1) matters more than a better ranking.

noai_*.question: What does the workload cost with no agent and no runtime in the loop?
noai_*.why: A floor. Without it there is no way to say how much of a trial is irreducible work.
noai_*.produced: 31 no-AI replay runs of the ChemGraph and AtomAgents work.

INVALID_port_conflict.question: —
INVALID_port_conflict.why: Kept deliberately, named so it cannot be mistaken for data.
INVALID_port_conflict.produced: A run invalidated by a vLLM port collision with another user on a shared node.

bench_gpu_eviction.question: When a GPU is already occupied, can the residency actor take it?
bench_gpu_eviction.why: This is the failure behind the project's negative end-to-end result. On the aligned campaign 16 of 16 model prefetches failed, 10 of them in under a millisecond with 'Cannot start qwen_32b: GPUs [0,1,2,3] occupied by qwen_72b. Call stop_model first.' The predictor was frequently right; its answer had nowhere to go, because all three models declare the same four GPUs. Everything else in Tandem is downstream of whether this works.
bench_gpu_eviction.produced: One GPU, two 68.28 GB engines that cannot coexist on a 96 GB card. Control (orchestrator.start_model): model_b crashed after 30.04 s with model_a holding 84023 MiB — contention confirmed. Tandem (actor.activate): ok=true, GPU freed, model_b served coherently (probe returned ' Paris. The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C.'). But it evicted by STOP, not park: 'park raised HTTPError: 404 Not Found for /sleep?level=1', forcing a 1256.63 s cold boot where a wake is ~2 s.
bench_gpu_eviction.claim: The actor takes an occupied GPU — the thing that failed 16/16 times. But with the sleep endpoint missing it downgrades to stop and throws away the retention benefit, and the park-vs-stop choice was being made by a missing HTTP route rather than by the arbitrator's budget callback.
bench_gpu_eviction.note: Run on ONE GPU deliberately: the property under test is contention, not scale, and the partition was 23/24 allocated all day. The control arm is load-bearing — a green tandem arm on a free GPU would look identical. Two harness flaws found and fixed: the control used start_model, which has no occupancy guard and merely crashes, rather than start_model_measured, whose guard at model_orchestrator.py:597-598 produces the recorded error; and a_alive was read as get_running_model() is not None, which cannot tell 'model_a survived' from 'model_b is now running'. The 404 was a live defect in the production tandem arm, not just the harness.
